output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation, not a v4.18 fault. The last 26 weeks average 0.354% with a normal upper edge of 0.482%, and 0.411% sits inside that. Earlier weeks reached 0.51%, 0.47% and 0.45%. Those were investigated and no fault was found. The dashboard matches raw log counts and hasn't changed, so it isn't a counting artefact. The "new pods error at nearly twice the rate" finding is a rollout warm-up effect. New pods start with a cold cache and time out against the replica. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image. It adds only 10–20 errors per rollout, far short of the roughly 2,000 extra errors that week. No one has compared pods of the same age on different versions, so v4.18 isn't fully cleared. The replica move and partner-sync traffic remain untested, but nothing requires acting on them. Customer impact is nil: bookings were flat and there were no complaints. Recommendation: don't roll back, and never mute the alerting. Note the week at ops review and apply the standard check to next week. If next week is above 0.48%, or the burn-rate page fires, open an incident and look at the replica and partner-sync timing then.
